items.stem: Why do enterprises often choose a permissioned blockchain over a public one for a consortium?

options.text: They need known, identity-verified participants and confidential data between specific members
options.rationale: Correct: permissioned networks provide identity and confidentiality controls.

options.text: Public chains cannot store any data
options.rationale: Public chains store data; the issue is confidentiality and identity.

options.text: Permissioned chains are always cheaper to run
options.rationale: Cost is not the defining reason.

options.text: Public chains are illegal for businesses

items.explanation: Correct: permissioned networks provide identity and confidentiality controls.

items.stem: Which TWO mechanisms let a permissioned network keep data visible only to specific members? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Channels that restrict a ledger to a subset of participants
Private data collections sharing only hashes on the shared ledger
Publishing all data to a public explorer
Giving every member the same admin certificate
options.rationale: That removes access control, not adds privacy.

items.stem: When is a permissioned blockchain the wrong choice for a consortium?

options.text: When a single trusted operator and a shared database would meet the trust and audit needs
options.rationale: Correct: if trust is centralisable, a database is simpler and sufficient.

options.text: Whenever more than two companies are involved
options.rationale: Member count alone does not decide this.

items.explanation: Correct: if trust is centralisable, a database is simpler and sufficient.
